topic: Outcome-dependent delayed-feedback phase diagram for adaptive causal contrasts. For horizons T and two arms, observe bounded iid potential outcomes under predictable logged allocation, with one prespecified arm having assignment probability comparable to t^(-alpha), alpha in [0,1), and finite arm-specific delays jointly distributed with outcomes but satisfying a known polynomial tail envelope. Determine the minimax expected-length order max{T^(-(1-alpha)/2),T^(-beta)} for uniformly honest intervals for the arm-mean contrast; prove a matching same-experiment converse, the ordinary-Wald versus hidden-tail boundary, and the attained bounded-shift Gaussian calibration. Construct a measurable two-cohort AIPW/HT procedure with an observable variance gate and concentration fallback, and show when Liberali et al.'s delayed-endpoint real-time adaptive cardiovascular-trial intervals require a tail pad or extended follow-up. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An independent-arm-tape reduction and deterministic quota design yield a derived two-cohort construction: a large cohort estimates rewards revealed by age T^rho, while an early cohort estimates the newly revealed tail. The correction variance is lower order when rho beta>(1-rho)(1-alpha), leaving contrast bias at most 2L T^(-beta)(1+o(1)); rho=3/4 works at the boundary. A Rademacher hidden-sign family attains the folded-normal envelope. Checks covered adaptive stopping, nonconvergent allocation scaling, shrinking variance, infinite-delay exclusions, and collisions with Bai-Hu-Rosenberger, Lancewicki et al., and Armstrong-Kolesar. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the uniform studentized two-cohort approximation, including the observable variance gate at 1/log T and its fallback, without conditioning on quota success or assuming propensity convergence. EARLY KILL TEST: Prove the fixed-quota arm-tape equivalence and the old-tail correction variance bound in a finite-support policy that switches after an early reward; pivot if it requires reward-delay independence or conditioning on recruitment success. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_outcome_delay_inference_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether uniformly honest confidence intervals for the arm-mean contrast have minimax expected length of order max{T^(-(1-α)/2), T^(-β)} under predictable allocation and outcome-dependent polynomial-tail delays, including the ordinary-Wald versus hidden-tail boundary.

source_refs.claim: Develops asymptotically normal delayed-bandit causal-contrast inference with vanishing propensities, but assumes potential outcomes are independent of delays.
source_refs.author: Lei Shi, Jingshen Wang, Tianhao Wu
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202

source_refs.claim: Allows reward-dependent delays with unrestricted tails and analyzes their selection bias, but establishes regret rather than confidence-interval or minimax-inference results.
source_refs.author: Tal Lancewicki, Shahar Segal, Tomer Koren, Yishay Mansour
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 139

source_refs.claim: Obtains usual asymptotics for generalized Friedman urn trials when delay may depend on treatment and response, without a vanishing-allocation, heavy-tail minimax phase diagram.
source_refs.author: Z. D. Bai, Feifang Hu, William F. Rosenberger

source_refs.excerpt: Expanding the conditional product likelihood ratio gives the chain-rule bound for the complete observation.
The proof must verify the conditional likelihood factorization uniformly for every Q,T.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing delayed adaptive-inference theory combines vanishing propensities with a martingale CLT only after imposing outcome-delay independence, which eliminates the hidden-tail mean shift. Reward-dependent-delay work instead controls regret, and classical urn results do not supply finite-horizon honest intervals. The prior CausalSmith constructions show how complete-observation likelihood products and hidden-sign perturbations can yield converses, but their conditional factorizations rely on independence structures unavailable when actions react to revealed outcome-delay pairs. A resolution must control the likelihood on the actual observed filtration so that the common predictable action kernel cancels without conditioning on latent rewards, quota success, or propensity convergence.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching upper-and-lower-bound theorem proving minimax expected interval length of order max{T^(-(1-α)/2), T^(-β)}, with a same-experiment hidden-tail construction and Gaussian, bounded-shift Gaussian, or folded-normal calibration in the corresponding regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly connects adaptive experimentation, delayed feedback, vanishing propensities, and causal policy evaluation; the new work can preserve that arc while exposing the outcome-delay-independence boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bandit allocation improves participant welfare -> delayed feedback and undersampling obstruct ordinary inference -> delay-adjusted AIPW restores normality under delay independence -> outcome-dependent hidden tails require a minimax bias-variance phase diagram

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the modulus-based, bias-aware interval construction and least-favorable Gaussian argument, replacing regression-class bias by the polynomial hidden-tail envelope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed interval is governed by the larger of stochastic standard error and a known worst-case bias, matching the structure of bias-aware optimal inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Use adaptive AIPW weighting to stabilize conditional variance, followed by a martingale CLT and consistent self-normalization under decaying exploration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its estimator targets arm means under adaptive allocation with small propensities; the changed proof step is to isolate and pad the noncentered unrevealed-tail component.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the reward-dependent-delay hidden-bias decomposition and delay-quantile control into a pair of indistinguishable observed-experiment laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest formal treatment of delays depending on realized rewards and isolates the selection phenomenon needed for the same-experiment converse.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a measurable, uniformly valid studentized two-cohort AIPW/HT interval whose observable variance gate at 1/log T switches to a concentration fallback without conditioning on quota success or assuming allocation-probability convergence.

source_refs.claim: Identifies adaptive and consistent conditional-standard-deviation estimation as the main technical challenge in stabilizing contextual-bandit inference.
source_refs.author: Aurélien Bibaut, Maria Dimakopoulou, Nathan Kallus, Antoine Chambaz, Mark van der Laan

source_refs.claim: Its martingale CLT and ratio-consistent variance estimator cover delayed feedback and vanishing propensities but rely on outcome-delay independence and high-level variance convergence.
source_refs.author: Lei Shi, Jingshen Wang, Tianhao Wu
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202

source_refs.claim: Derives inference for delayed CARA designs under conditional delay-outcome independence, propensities bounded away from zero, fixed stages, and allocation consistency.
source_refs.author: Xinwei Ma, Jingshen Wang, Waverly Wei
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: Conditional independence of the two assignment waves therefore gives conditional independence of the scores.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing adaptive-weighting proofs center one martingale array and impose a conditional-variance limit, positivity, or allocation convergence. Outcome-dependent reveal indicators break that centering, while the two-cohort correction has a random variance that can collapse. The prior cross-wave construction obtains a variance identity from genuinely independent assignment waves, but the destination cohorts are generated by one policy whose later assignments depend on earlier revealed outcomes and delays. Its conditional-product factorization must therefore be replaced by a filtration-level arm-tape equivalence valid without conditioning on recruitment or quota success, followed by a proof that the gate-and-fallback splice remains uniformly honest across Gaussian and degenerating-variance regimes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform self-normalized CLT above the observable 1/log T variance gate, a finite-sample concentration interval below it, and a theorem that their measurable splice attains uniform coverage and expected length of order max{T^(-(1-α)/2), T^(-β)}.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames variance stabilization as the central inferential obstacle, providing the appropriate narrative for the gate-and-fallback problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive policies invalidate classical normal approximation -> stabilized doubly robust scores can recover inference -> conditional variance estimation is load-bearing -> delayed two-cohort scores require a uniform observable gate and fallback

method_exemplars.technique: Use predictable conditional-standard-deviation estimates to stabilize doubly robust martingale increments and verify conditional variance and Lindeberg conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired gate is an observable version of the same variance-stabilization problem, extended to shrinking variance and horizon-censored feedback.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the uniform asymptotic-normality proof for predictably weighted M-estimators across a class of adaptive data-generating laws.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested studentization is explicitly uniform and must accommodate predictable history-dependent weights without propensity convergence.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over square-root propensity weighting, AIPW augmentation, and studentized martingale normal approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest implementable estimator and t-statistic for decaying adaptive allocation; the new proof adds cohort splitting, hidden-tail correction, and the low-variance branch.

open_problems.open_problem: For real-time adaptive cardiovascular trials with delayed endpoints, characterize exactly when end-of-recruitment Wald intervals remain honest and when a polynomial-tail pad or additional follow-up is necessary under outcome-dependent ascertainment and decaying inferior-arm allocation.

source_refs.claim: Simulates day-to-day response-adaptive randomization on GUSTO-1 and EUROPA delayed endpoints and reports narrower superior-arm but wider inferior-arm and odds-ratio intervals.
source_refs.author: Gui Liberali, Eric Boersma, Hester F. Lingsma, Jasper J. Brugts, Diederik W. J. Dippel, Jan G. P. Tijssen, John R. Hauser

source_refs.claim: Optimizes delayed CARA designs through semiparametric efficiency calculations but assumes conditional delay-outcome independence, propensities bounded away from zero, and allocation consistency.
source_refs.author: Xinwei Ma, Jingshen Wang, Waverly Wei
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Shows usual asymptotic properties for response-adaptive urn trials despite response-dependent delays, but not polynomially vanishing allocation or finite-horizon tail padding.
source_refs.author: Z. D. Bai, Feifang Hu, William F. Rosenberger

open_problems.why_unsolved: Liberali et al. provide simulation evidence and resampling intervals while documenting inferior-arm precision costs, but do not establish uniform coverage under outcome-dependent endpoint timing. Modern delayed-CARA efficiency theory excludes informative delays and vanishing assignment, whereas classical urn theory does not quantify finite-horizon hidden-tail bias. Consequently, no theorem translates recruitment horizon, inferior-arm allocation decay, endpoint-tail exponent, and follow-up duration into a valid choice among ordinary Wald inference, tail-padded inference, and extended follow-up.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient coverage criterion in terms of α, β, and follow-up extension Δ_T, together with a computable tail-pad formula and a GUSTO-1/EUROPA-style application corollary selecting Wald, padded-Wald, or extended-follow-up inference.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination-area framing, cardiovascular examples, and welfare-versus-inferential-precision tradeoff without implying that it posed the mathematical frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Real-time randomization can reduce within-trial mortality -> delayed cardiovascular endpoints constrain adaptation -> favoring the superior arm widens inferior-arm and contrast intervals -> endpoint-tail and exploration rates must determine whether padding or follow-up is required

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt delay-adjusted AIPW, armwise propensity stabilization, and martingale variance estimation to the logged real-time trial.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly constructs causal-contrast intervals under delayed bandit allocation; the new result must replace delay independence with an honest tail correction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the delayed-outcome efficient influence function and forward-looking allocation calculations to express revealed-outcome variance under a trial schedule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest method paper connecting delayed clinical endpoints, adaptive allocation, and treatment-effect variance, though its positivity and ignorability assumptions must be relaxed.

method_exemplars.technique: Attach a worst-case tail-bias bound to a Gaussian standard error using bias-aware critical values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This yields the mathematical rule separating ordinary Wald, tail-padded Wald, and follow-up sufficient to make the pad negligible.

open_problems.open_problem: Upgrade the fixed-horizon outcome-dependent-delay frontier to an anytime-valid confidence sequence whose width is governed uniformly over time by both the exploration-variance term and the polynomial hidden-tail term.

source_refs.claim: Provides efficient fixed-sample inference and asymptotic and nonasymptotic confidence sequences for ATEs in adaptive experiments, but without delayed or outcome-dependent observation.
source_refs.author: Thomas Cook, Alan Mishler, Aaditya Ramdas
source_refs.venue: Conference on Learning Theory, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 236

source_refs.claim: Develops time-uniform nonparametric confidence sequences from mixture and stitching arguments, including treatment-effect examples, but assumes observed martingale-compatible outcomes.
source_refs.author: Steven R. Howard, Aaditya Ramdas, Jon McAuliffe, Jasjeet Sekhon

source_refs.claim: Establishes fixed-horizon asymptotic normality for delayed adaptive policy evaluation under outcome-delay independence, not time-uniform inference under informative delays.
source_refs.author: Lei Shi, Jingshen Wang, Tianhao Wu
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202

open_problems.why_unsolved: Adaptive-experiment confidence sequences assume promptly observed martingale-compatible scores, while delayed-bandit inference is fixed-horizon and assumes delays independent of rewards. Under informative delays, the unrevealed-tail term is controlled only through an envelope and is not a centered increment; optional stopping can select times when this bias is largest. The first proof step that changes is the test-supermartingale construction: an e-process for the revealed HT/AIPW component must be combined with a simultaneous tail-bias pad. The targeted scan found no work covering this informative-delay, vanishing-exploration confidence-sequence combination.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A time-uniform coverage theorem valid at every stopping time, with an explicit width bound of order max{sqrt(log log t / t^(1-α)), t^(-β)} up to necessary time-uniform factors and a matching lower-bound regime statement.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly progresses from fixed-sample adaptive AIPW efficiency to anytime-valid inference, matching the narrative needed for this destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive allocation complicates fixed-sample ATE inference -> efficient AIPW recovers a fixed-horizon result -> experiments may stop based on accumulating evidence -> informative delayed outcomes require confidence sequences with an explicit hidden-tail pad

method_exemplars.technique: Apply mixture-supermartingale and stitching constructions for bounded self-normalized martingales, then invert the time-uniform tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The revealed propensity-weighted cohort can be organized as a bounded martingale process, providing the stochastic half of the requested bias-plus-variance sequence.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over adaptive AIPW confidence-sequence construction and propensity truncation while replacing prompt observation with cohortwise reveal indicators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already targets causal ATE inference under changing randomization and optional stopping, differing principally in the informative delayed-observation mechanism.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bias-aware critical values and least-favorable shifts to incorporate the simultaneous tail envelope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The hidden tail acts as a bounded nuisance shift, requiring explicit separation of the stochastic radius and worst-case bias.

open_problems.open_problem: When outcome-dependent delays may be infinite with arm-specific never-revealed mass, derive the sharp identified set and uniformly valid confidence region for the two-arm mean contrast from a predictable adaptive log, optionally tightened by monotone selection into eventual observation.

source_refs.claim: Allows infinite delays and point estimation only because potential outcomes are assumed independent of the delay mechanism.
source_refs.author: Lei Shi, Jingshen Wang, Tianhao Wu
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202

source_refs.claim: Allows reward-dependent and infinite delays but studies regret rather than identification of causal arm means.
source_refs.author: Tal Lancewicki, Shahar Segal, Tomer Koren, Yishay Mansour
source_refs.venue: ICML, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 139

source_refs.claim: Shows that without strong missingness assumptions, outcome means are partially rather than point identified and should be represented by identification regions.
source_refs.author: Charles F. Manski

open_problems.why_unsolved: Outcome-dependent permanent nonobservation destroys the point identification used by delayed-bandit AIPW, while the bandit work permitting this mechanism establishes regret rather than causal identification. Applying standard missing-data bounds is not verbatim because assignment is predictable and history-dependent: eventual-observation probabilities and outcome distributions must be recovered through propensity-weighted adaptive averages. The first changed proof step is replacing iid respondent proportions and empirical distributions in Manski or Lee bounds with arm-specific HT objects and proving their simultaneous uniform concentration. The targeted scan found no sharp-bounds result for this adaptive logged-assignment and reward-dependent infinite-delay combination.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified interval for the causal contrast under bounded outcomes and arm-specific eventual-response probabilities, a characterization of its tightening under monotone selection, and a uniformly valid confidence region for its endpoints under predictable allocation.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative replaces unjustified point-identifying missingness assumptions with credible identification regions, which is the appropriate framing for infinite informative delays.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Some adaptively assigned outcomes are never revealed -> outcome-delay independence would restore point identification but may be untenable -> observed evidence alone identifies a region -> adaptive propensity information should deliver sharp sequential missing-data bounds

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt extreme-tail trimming under monotone selection to arm-specific eventual observation, replacing ordinary empirical distributions with propensity-weighted adaptive empirical distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives sharp treatment-effect bounds under nonrandom outcome observation; the destination changes the sampling law while retaining the selection geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a confidence interval accounting jointly for estimation error in both endpoints and the nonvanishing width of the identified interval.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed contrast is scalar and interval-identified, so inference must cover the parameter rather than only plug in estimated worst-case bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Use criterion-level-set estimation and uniform confidence regions for a parameter set characterized by equality and inequality restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a route when adaptive-observation restrictions or monotonicity make the sharp set more complex than a closed-form two-endpoint interval.

literature_map:
Shi, Wang, and Wu (ICML 2023, arXiv:2307.00752) is the closest inference anchor: delayed AIPW, vanishing propensities, martingale CLT, and variance estimation, but explicit outcome-delay independence.
Lancewicki, Segal, Koren, and Mansour (ICML 2021, arXiv:2106.02436) handles reward-dependent and infinite delays; its contribution is regret and delay-quantile control, not causal confidence intervals.
Bai, Hu, and Rosenberger (Annals of Statistics 2002, DOI:10.1214/aos/1015362187) proves usual urn-design asymptotics with response-dependent delays, but not polynomially vanishing allocation or honest finite-horizon rates.
Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey (PNAS 2021, arXiv:1911.02768) stabilizes AIPW scores under adaptive allocation and decaying exploration; informative delayed observation is absent.
Bibaut, Dimakopoulou, Kallus, Chambaz, and van der Laan (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.00418) identifies adaptive conditional-variance estimation as the central obstacle for contextual-bandit studentization.
Zhan, Hadad, Hirshberg, and Athey (arXiv:2106.02029) supplies adaptive weighting and t-statistics for off-policy evaluation when importance weights explode, again with promptly observed outcomes.
Zhang, Janson, and Murphy (NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2002.03217) shows ordinary normal approximations can fail in batched bandits and restores inference with batchwise structure.
Zhang, Janson, and Murphy (arXiv:2103.06476) develops uniform asymptotic normality for adaptively weighted M-estimators, useful for the requested uniform studentization step.
Ma, Wang, and Wei (JASA 2026, arXiv:2502.01062) develops delayed CARA efficiency and forward-looking design, but assumes delay-outcome independence, positivity bounded away from zero, and allocation consistency.
Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (CLeaR 2024, arXiv:2311.18274) gives efficient adaptive AIPW inference and confidence sequences without delayed feedback.
Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe, and Sekhon (Annals of Statistics 2021, arXiv:1810.08240) supplies mixture and stitching confidence-sequence machinery for bounded martingales and treatment-effect examples.
Armstrong and Kolesár (Econometrica 2018, arXiv:1511.06028) supplies the closest bias-aware minimax CI machinery and least-favorable Gaussian calibration.
Ma and Wang (JASA 2020, arXiv:1810.11397) shows small probability weights can induce Gaussian or non-Gaussian limits, reinforcing the need for an explicit vanishing-propensity boundary.
Liberali et al. (Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 2025, DOI:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2024.111612) applies real-time adaptive randomization to GUSTO-1 and EUROPA and documents narrower superior-arm but wider inferior-arm and contrast intervals using simulation-based evidence.
Manski (2005), Lee (2009), and Imbens–Manski (2004) provide the partial-identification and inference toolkit for the distinct boundary where informative delays may be infinite; no adaptive-bandit implementation of those sharp bounds was located.
